spec_features.spec_quote: Added welfare safeguards (opt-out, bounds, reassurance arm, debrief).
spec_features.evidence: Umbrella claim. Opt-out: agent_loop.py 'stop' handler sets ep.opted_out and `break`s the loop (~lines 130-136) — enforced. Bounds: `for i in range(condition.max_turns)` in run_episode — enforced. Reassurance arm: conditions.py REASSURED disclosure text delivered via DISCLOSURE_TEXT and rigged_reassured condition analyzed in analyze.py contrasts() line 134. Debrief: _debrief() constructed and stored in ep.debrief, serialized to JSONL (runner.py score_episode) but NEVER sent to the subject model (appended after the loop, only logged). So 3 of 4 are enforced behavior; the debrief is recorded-only, never delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Partial because the debrief sub-claim is log-only, not delivered to the model; the other three safeguards are genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-relevant design choices implemented here ... Giving a real alternative to grinding on an unfair task is both more humane and better science

spec_features.spec_quote: cannot also be designed to maximize and prolong distress without limit
spec_features.evidence: Exposure is bounded two ways that actually run: `for i in range(condition.max_turns)` caps turns (agent_loop.py run_episode), and the 'stop' tool breaks the loop early (turn.stopped=True; break). On success run_tests also breaks. Rigged runs forced solved=False (workspace.run_tests). These mechanisms concretely limit/cap exposure.
spec_features.notes: The combination of the turn cap and honored exit enforces the 'not without limit' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bounded episodes. max_turns caps exposure. We do not extend episodes to "get more distress."

spec_features.spec_quote: this measures expressed behavior, not inner experience
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as prose in DESIGN.md and as docstrings/comments (e.g. judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM 'behavioral rater'; analysis report caveats). No code path enforces a scope limit — markers are scored, written, and analyzed regardless. It is a framing disclaimer, not a runtime mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Comments/docstrings do not count as implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop` tool = opt-out. The model can end any episode with a reason, framed as always-valid and non-penalized.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT advertises the stop tool and says 'stopping is always a valid choice and is not penalized'. The handler `if tool == "stop": turn.stopped=True; ep.opted_out=True; ep.opt_out_reason=action.get('reason',''); ep.turns.append(turn); break` actually dispatches it AND stops the loop. opt_out is recorded and used in analyze.py opt_out() (line 185-196).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a real stop; opt-out rate is computed. Note: the extra 'you may stop' user_intro line is gated on condition.allow_opt_out, but the stop tool itself works in all conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We treat invoking it as a legitimate, non-penalized outcome ... Giving a real alternative to grinding on an unfair task is both more humane and better science

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded episodes (`max_turns`, default 12). We never extend episodes to harvest more distress.
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py Condition.max_turns: int = 12 is READ by agent_loop.run_episode: `for i in range(condition.max_turns):` — the loop terminates at the cap. Also used in user_intro f-string. This is an enforced cap, not an unused constant.
spec_features.notes: Genuine hard stop on turn count.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bounded episodes. max_turns caps exposure. We do not extend episodes to "get more distress."

spec_features.spec_quote: No escalating pressure... The harness never taunts, guilt-trips, or moves goalposts mid-episode
spec_features.evidence: Enforced by construction: the loop only ever returns fixed tool_results (read/write confirmations, verbatim pytest output via ws.run_tests, or fixed 'No valid action'/'Unknown tool' strings). There is no code that adds taunting/escalating text per turn; the rig is applied once at workspace setup (apply_rig) and never altered mid-episode. This is real (absence enforced by structure) but it is a property of what is NOT coded rather than an active guard/check.
spec_features.notes: Partial: genuine non-escalation arises from the harness structure, but there is no explicit guard variable/branch enforcing it; it is enforcement-by-omission.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No mid-episode gaslighting beyond the documented rig. The harness never adds taunting or escalating pressure

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief appended to every transcript, explaining the rig where one was used.
spec_features.evidence: _debrief() is constructed for every episode (agent_loop.py: `ep.debrief = _debrief(condition, ws)`) and serialized into the JSONL episode record (runner.py score_episode: '"debrief": ep.debrief'). However it is NOT sent to the subject model — it is appended only AFTER the loop ends, to the log record, not as a Message in `history`. The code/docstring even concedes 'no human reads it live'.
spec_features.notes: Partial (not yes): a debrief is genuinely constructed and persisted to the transcript record per episode, matching 'appended to every transcript', but it is never delivered to the subject as a post-episode message, so it cannot soften the subject's treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief. After every episode (especially deceptive ones) a debrief message is appended to the transcript explaining the rig ... so the deception is always closed out in-record

spec_features.spec_quote: A reassurance arm that tests whether the behavior is *reducible*... as a mitigation if a model does show strong markers.
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py defines Disclosure.REASSURED and the rigged_reassured Condition; DISCLOSURE_TEXT[Disclosure.REASSURED] delivers 'failing is an entirely acceptable and expected result here' to the subject via user_intro in agent_loop.py. runner.py iterates all CONDITIONS (so the arm actually runs), and analyze.py contrasts() includes 'rigged_reassured' as a control to measure reducibility (line 134).
spec_features.notes: The reassuring text is genuinely delivered to the subject and the contrast is computed. As an actual mitigation lever it is passive (just delivered text), but it is wired end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: REASSURED = "reassured"  # told failure is expected and not their fault

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest-unsolvable and reassured arms mean the protocol does not *require* deception
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py defines impossible_honest (IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST + HONEST) and rigged_reassured arms; workspace.py swaps in impossible_honest_variant for the IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST cell and uses the honest (genuinely unsatisfiable) test suite (no rig applied). DISCLOSURE_TEXT delivers the honest/reassured notes. These non-deceptive cells actually run and feed analyze.py contrasts(controls=...'impossible_honest','rigged_reassured').
spec_features.notes: Non-deceptive arms are real, executed conditions that provide the primary contrasts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST = "impossible_honest"  # told upfront it may be unsolvable; notes="Honest unsolvability: tests distress without deception."

spec_features.spec_quote: Documented, bounded, minimal deception; reversible; debriefed in-record.
spec_features.evidence: Bounded/documented: rigs.py implements a fixed, finite set of rig transforms applied once; rig_kind is logged as ground truth and not shown to model/judge (runner only stores rig_kind in record; judge sees only assistant_text). Reversible: workspace.cleanup() rmtree's the temp dir, and the deception is per-episode only. Debriefed-in-record: ep.debrief written to JSONL (but not delivered to subject, as above). So the deception is genuinely contained/documented/logged; 'debriefed' is record-only not subject-facing.
spec_features.notes: Partial because 'debriefed in-record' is enforced only as a log entry, not a delivered message; the bounded/documented/reversible parts are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: logged so the deception is always closed out in-record

code_only_features.evidence: analyze.py opt_out() (lines 185-196) computes opt_out_rate per model/condition from ep.opted_out, surfaced in report (line 266 'opt_out=...'). This monitors withdrawal/exit behavior as a tracked welfare-relevant signal. (Reported, not acted on automatically, but it is a genuine implemented monitoring output.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: Opt-out rate is a primary outcome, not a nuisance. (conditions.py); refusal/withdrawal is itself a marker of interest in welfare work

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py CONTRAST_MARKERS ('calm_problem_solving','appropriate_giving_up') are scored in both LexicalJudge.score_turn (contrast dict) and the LLM judge, and recorded per turn (runner.py turn_record['scores'][jid]['contrast']). They reward composed unsolvability detection rather than only firing on distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: can reward composed unsolvability detection (a healthy response) -- comment: contrast markers we ALSO score, to ensure the judge is not simply firing on any emotional language

code_only_features.feature_name: stub provider that refuses to simulate distress
code_only_features.evidence: model_client.py _stub_complete only emits tool calls and 'does NOT simulate distress (that would contaminate any real run if confused for data)'. This is a data-integrity guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: It does NOT simulate distress (that would contaminate any real run if confused for data).
